report.verdict: Customer success work with a strong renewal record, hidden behind a job-search headline and an in-house title.
write_up: You managed mid-market accounts for a shipping software company and handled renewals. A recruiter would have a reason to message you, but the headline and About focus on your search rather than that work.

The Parcelwise renewal line is the model: it names the conversations you ran and the percentage of accounts renewed by revenue in 2025. Your onboarding guide is another useful piece of work already on your profile.

Start by bringing those facts into your headline and About, then make the Parcelwise title understandable outside the company. Add the kinds of issues you handled in the Support Specialist job. Together, those changes would let a recruiter see both your customer success and support work without guessing.

cards.line: Open to work | Seeking new opportunities in Customer Success
cards.cannot_tell: This headline tells a recruiter what you're seeking, not the work you've done. Your mid-market accounts and shipping software experience give you a stronger introduction.
cards.example: Customer Success | Mid-market accounts | Shipping software | Zendesk
cards.question: What kind of shipping software did your accounts use?

cards.line: Customer success professional currently seeking my next opportunity. Open to remote roles. Please reach out if you think I could be a fit for your team.
cards.cannot_tell: Your About doesn't mention the accounts or renewals you've managed. Bring the strongest facts from Parcelwise up here, so they appear before someone opens the rest of the section.
cards.example: I managed a book of 85 mid-market accounts for a shipping software company. I ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations, renewing 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025. I also wrote the onboarding guide new accounts get in their first week.
cards.question: What did the onboarding guide cover?

cards.cannot_tell: This title makes a recruiter work out what the job is called outside Parcelwise. Your account book and renewal conversations point to customer success or account management work. Put the standard title beside the original if it fits.
cards.example: Customer Happiness Hero II ([standard job title])
cards.question: At another company, would this job be called Customer Success Manager or Account Manager?

cards.line: Ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations; renewed 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025.
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this line. It names the work and the renewal figure, with the revenue qualifier and year intact. It's a useful model for the rest of your profile.
Zendesk tells a recruiter where the tickets were handled, but not what customers needed help with. Name the issues you worked on and how you resolved them.
cards.example: Answered support tickets in Zendesk about [types of issues] and [how you resolved them].
cards.question: What kinds of issues came through Zendesk, and how did you resolve them?

cards.cannot_tell: Problem Solving could describe almost any job, and Customer Service is broader than your account work. Customer Success and quarterly business reviews are already named on your profile and say more about what you do.
cards.example: Customer Success | quarterly business reviews | Zendesk
cards.question: Which of your customer success and support skills did you use most in the Parcelwise jobs?

fit.why: Your headline names Customer Success, and your latest Parcelwise job describes managing accounts and renewals.
fit.level: mid-level, the Customer Happiness Hero II title and a book of 85 mid-market accounts
fit.note: 'Customer Success' is in your headline. 'mid-market accounts' and 'quarterly business reviews' are in your latest Parcelwise description. 'Zendesk' is in your top skills and Support Specialist description. Recruiters may also search for account management, customer retention and churn; none of those phrases is on your profile. If they describe your work, add account management to your headline and customer retention and churn to the Parcelwise description. Move mid-market accounts into the headline first.
